result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse returns `refreshTokenResponse` (a zod safeParse result), and in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` followed by `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. This stores the SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}) as the credential key rather than `key.data`, so the persisted shape no longer matches googleCredentialSchema on subsequent loads. The mechanism described is verifiable directly in the diff.

judged_text: The Google token refresh persists the zod safeParse wrapper as the credential key: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}) but `data: { key }` stores that wrapper object instead of `key.data`. The stored credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}}, so on the next load googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws (access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date are now nested under .data) and every Google Calendar operation for that user fails; the refresh itself reports success, so credentials are silently corrupted for all deployments (no env flags required) within ~1 hour of deploy and require manual DB surgery or user re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which will store the wrapper object as the credential key instead of the actual credential payload. This differs from other usages in the diff (e.g., Office365/Salesforce) that treat the return as a wrapper and access `.data`. This would corrupt the stored credential structure for Google by nesting expected fields under `.data`.
